web.title: The ATO Knows About Your Overseas Bank Accounts
web.description:
For many, part of living or working abroad means that they have a bank account with a foreign bank.

## The tax background to CRS for expat Australians
##### **The ATO already knows about your foreign bank account!**
The ATO knows your overseas account number. They know the closing balance of your account, and they know every detail about every single deposit into your overseas bank account.

**How do they know?**

And as a result you can bet your bottom dollar that the ATO already knows about your foreign bank account, about all the details of your account, about your closing balance along with all of the details of all the income that you have had paid into that account.

## $1 Billion of funding issued to the ATO to combat tax avoidance
What this means for Australian taxpayers and Aussie expats, is that you should assume that the ATO already knows everything about your foreign bank and financial accounts.

## I have a foreign bank account and have not declared it to the ATO. What should I do?
There’s also reasons why an Australian might not be required to report that account to the ATO on their Australian tax return, the principal reasons of which include that:

1. the person may not be an Australian tax resident and therefore does not have an obligation to report their foreign income or their foreign account to Australia, or
2. the person may be an Australian tax resident but they did not earn any foreign income at all and thus had nothing to report.

**But what should I do?** Well, firstly, you should review your residency status to confirm whether you are a tax resident of Australia or a non-resident. That’s a massive difference.

For other’s take a look here: [Am I an Australian resident for tax purposes? 10 factors to consider](https://www.expattaxes.com.au/australian-resident-for-tax-purposes-10-factors/).

Why?

The latter of which will be penalised like no tomorrow!
